newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Japanese in arbitrage play in Singapore rubber.
newsitem.headline: Japanese in arbitrage play in Singapore rubber.

text.p: A Japanese dealer was said to be engaged in buying rubber grades across the board by midday on Friday to take advantage of the arbitrage between the Singapore and Tokyo rubber markets, dealers said.
The buying drove up prices of RSS3 and RSS1 grade rubber, with rubber brokers still checking the volume of TSR20 rubber the dealer has reportedly bought, they said.

"One Japanese dealer has been seen buying across the board. He is the only buyer in the market and apparently wants to play the arbitrage of his positions between the Singapore and Tokyo markets," a trader said.
"The broker did most of his buying in the ring sessions. Otherwise, trading would have been quiet," a dealer said.
Traders said they were waiting for fresh leads in the afternoon and to see if the buying by the Japanese dealer would continue.

At 0430 GMT, June RSS3 prices surged and were seen at 116.00 U.S. cents a kg from its settlement on Thursday of 111.75 cents. July RSS3 jumped to 116.50 U.S. cents a kg from 113.25 cents. June RSS1 prices also jumped and were seen at 166.50 Singapore cents (US$1.16) a kg from 161.25 cents.
